latest_semantic_finding.observation: The official test file defines a MockTransport implementing both httpx.BaseTransport and httpx.AsyncBaseTransport; its request handlers return httpx.Response objects directly. The synchronous and asynchronous binary-upload tests instantiate Groq/AsyncGroq with caller-supplied httpx clients whose transport is that MockTransport, then call client.post and receive the transport-produced response. The test fixture uses a dummy API key string.
latest_semantic_finding.inference: For the exact raw-response test path, the Groq SDK demonstrably supports an injected in-process transport that can satisfy the SDK request path without an external endpoint, so the ordinary HTTP dispatch identified in p1-sa-427 is not intrinsically tied to hosted network execution. The custom handler also does not validate bearer credentials, although the SDK constructor still requires a non-None key string. This removes the specific uncertainty about whether caller-supplied in-process transport is actually exercised by the SDK. It does not establish that a packaged high-level chat/completions response can be replayed through the same mechanism with full typed parsing or useful-outcome parity.

The observed custom-transport cases replay raw upload responses cast to httpx.Response rather than a high-level model response. No chat/completions fixture, response-package completeness, typed parsing, stream replay, semantic useful-outcome equivalence, production credential behavior, alternate provider, pricing/quota terms, or runtime trace was inspected. Therefore useful-outcome replayability and full Phase-1 acceptance remain unresolved.
